title: The Signature Physics Theorems Database — Theorems 1–3

The theorems themselves are public knowledge; the Signature layer adds JAH-system framings and applications. Theorem 1: Noether's Theorem. Statement: Every differentiable symmetry of a physical system's action yields a conservation law: time symmetry gives energy conservation, space symmetry gives momentum conservation. Signature framing: within the JAH Signature system this theorem is applied as a design rule — its statement is used verbatim, and Signature applications build on it without altering it. Theorem 2: Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle. Statement: Position and momentum cannot both be known to arbitrary precision: Δx·Δp ≥ ℏ/2, where ℏ is the reduced Planck constant. Signature framing: within the JAH Signature system this theorem is applied as a design rule — its statement is used verbatim, and Signature applications build on it without altering it. Theorem 3: Bell's Theorem. Statement: No local hidden-variable theory can reproduce all the statistical predictions of quantum mechanics; entanglement is irreducibly non-local. Signature framing: within the JAH Signature system this theorem is applied as a design rule — its statement is used verbatim, and Signature applications build on it without altering it.
